title: fix(app-shell): the formula editor writes the next field definition without the legacy `formula` key (objectui#12681)
body:
Fixes #12681
Clause-②: no (no export, prop or type changes; the draft stops carrying an own `formula` key)

## What changed

In the object designer, every edit in a formula field's **Formula (CEL)** editor brought up the red spec banner ("Unrecognized key(s) on this field: `formula`", followed by the pointer that the field "carries the retired `formula` key"), even on a field that stores only `expression`.

The editor's `onChange` migrated the legacy alias with `patchDef({ expression: …, formula: undefined, … })`. `patchDef` merges with a spread (`{ ...def, ...patch }`), so the draft field came out with an OWN `formula` property whose value is `undefined`. The page's live check (`validateMetadataDraft`, edit mode) parses the draft with the spec's strict field schema, which reports any own undeclared key as `unrecognized_keys` at `fields.NAME`, whatever its value. The pointer then rides on that issue. The wire drops `undefined`, so the save was always right, and the banner cleared once the autosave round-tripped.

The `onChange` now builds the field's next definition with the `formula` key left out (`const { formula: legacyFormula, ...rest } = def`). It writes that definition through `writeDef`, a new local helper that replaces the whole definition, so a key it leaves out is absent afterwards. `patchDef` is unchanged. `clientValidation.ts` is untouched, as the triage ruled: the client check is not silenced.

## Why the call site and not `patchDef` (the PM's hypothesis 1, measured)

- `patchDef` is `{ ...def, ...patch }`, so an own `undefined` survives. Confirmed.
- Probe: each key the inspector can write as `undefined` through `patchDef` (the `patchDef` / `onCommit` call sites in the file, plus `type`, `label`, `options`, `picklist`) was placed as an own `undefined` on a field and parsed with `ObjectSchema` from the installed `@objectstack/spec` (18.0.0-next.2). Only `formula` and `relationshipName` came back unrecognized. Every other key is declared, so an own `undefined` on it does nothing under the spec check.
- One existing pin relies on an own `undefined` surviving. *clears `returnType` when the inference degrades to unknown* asserts `'returnType' in p.fields.total`. A `patchDef`-level rule that an `undefined` patch deletes the key would change the draft shape at every `patchDef` caller, and that pin's premise, to repair one key.
- `relationshipName` is not a retired key. The spec does not declare it at all, so its control is refused even with a real value (see Acceptance notes). A delete-on-`undefined` rule would not make that control work.

So the narrowest correct fix is the one call site that patches a retired key to `undefined`. **Hypothesis 2:** the file has no other `patchDef` that writes a key from the retired-field-key tombstone registry (`indexed`, `referenceTo`, `formula`, `isSystem`, `sortOrder`), with or without a value. `formula` was the only one.

## Tests

- **New: `ObjectFieldInspector.formulaKeyOmitted-12681.test.tsx`.** It runs the real inspector inside a parent that feeds every patch back into the draft.
  - *THE PIN* types the card's keystrokes (` + 1`, one at a time), then clears the box and retypes. After each step it asserts three things: no own `formula` key; zero `unrecognized_keys` from `ObjectSchema`, the schema the client check loads for `object`; and zero issues at `fields.est_total` from `validateMetadataDraft('object', …, { mode: 'edit' })`, the console's own check.
  - *The legacy migration* covers a stored field carrying `formula`. Before the edit it is reported at `fields.est_total`, and the message names the Formula (CEL) editor. After one edit, `expression` holds the value, `formula` is absent, and both judges are clean.
  - A third case asserts that nothing else on the definition moves (an envelope `expression` with `meta`, `description`, `returnType`).
- **New: `ObjectFieldInspector.hostBanner-12681.test.tsx`.** It renders the real `MetadataResourceEditPage` with its registered object canvas, inspector and `object` config, as the objectui#10202 page tests do.
  - Autosave is off, so only the live check can clear the banner, and each case asserts that no PUT went out.
  - The pin records every result of the page's check and every banner state the DOM goes through (a `MutationObserver`). It judges them by subject: a line located at the field itself, never by message wording.
  - Clean field: no check and no banner state ever names `fields.est_total`. The lint line at `… → est_total → expression` does show for the dangling ` +`, which is the positive reading that the banner was live. The banner ends empty.
  - Legacy field: the line at the field is shown before the edit. No check of the edited draft names the field, and the banner ends empty.
  - The first version of this pin sampled one instant with autosave on, and it stayed GREEN under the ablation below. The page empties its issues on every draft change and re-checks 200ms later, so a sample can land in the gap, and the autosave clears the banner too. It was rewritten as above, and it now goes red.
- **Changed: `ObjectFieldInspector.test.tsx`.** *commits edits to `expression` and migrates the legacy `formula` key* now asserts `not.toHaveProperty('formula')`. Its old `toBeUndefined()` passes on an own `undefined`.

**Ablation.** The pre-fix `patchDef({ …, formula: undefined, … })` is put back through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which wraps the vitest run over the three files. Two legs, both identical, and each restore is proven by the tool (blob `0c3edb1a53dc` equals HEAD's, and `git diff HEAD` is empty). The run goes from `Tests 48 passed` to `Tests 5 failed | 43 passed`. Red on the mutation:
- both inspector pins (`expected { type: 'formula', … } to not have property "formula"`);
- both host pins (`expected [ 'fields → est_total' ] to deeply equal []`);
- the strengthened migration pin.

The direction is the usual one: the pins turn red.

## Browser reading

- Stack: objectstack `66d456d01`, `examples/app-crm`, run with `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh` as the backend only. The console comes from this branch through `apps/console` vite with `DEV_PROXY_TARGET`.
- Setup is the card's REST steps: the `com.qa.vrf` package (201) and `qavrf_job` with the clean formula field (200).
- Probe: open `/apps/crm_app/metadata/object/qavrf_job`, click `Est Total`, then in `#field-formula-est_total` press End and type ` + 1` at 80ms per key. A `MutationObserver` records every banner state for 6.5s.
- **This branch (2 runs):** no banner state at any point. The edit landed (`record.est_hours * 1.1 + 1`) and autosaved.
- **Control, same stack, pre-fix patch held on disk:** the banner showed `Fields → est_total: Unrecognized key(s) on this field: \`formula\`…` at about 1.06s, and it was gone at about 2.44s, after the autosave. This is the card's shape.
- **Legacy leg: NOT MEASURED in the browser.** The server refuses to store a field carrying `formula`, so a fresh backend cannot hold one. The host-page pin covers this leg.

## Local gates (HEAD `156dc7d`)

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' run build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 34 metadata-admin suites that name `ObjectFieldInspector`, `type: 'formula'` or the retired-`formula` pointer (the new pins included): `Test Files 34 passed (34)`, `Tests 442 passed (442)`, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists all three touched test files.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the four changed source and test files: exit 0, 0 errors. The 17 warnings are all on lines this PR does not touch.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, "4 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- CI check-runs: not yet concluded when this was written.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, class (a), reported for the seat to file: the lookup inspector's "Relationship name" control writes a key the spec refuses.**
  - `ObjectFieldInspector` renders a *Relationship name* text field for lookup types, and that field writes `relationshipName`. The installed `FieldSchema` does not declare it, and objectstack `main`'s `packages/spec/src` has no `relationshipName` either.
  - Measured on the stack above. Typing `jobs` into the field on `qavrf_rel.job` brings up `Fields → job: Unrecognized key(s) on this field: \`relationshipName\``, the autosave is refused, and the field stays *Unsaved*. Over REST, `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qavrf_rel?package=com.qa.vrf` with `relationshipName` on the lookup answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` (`unrecognized_keys` at `fields.job`); the same body without it answers 200.
  - Seam: `spec: FieldSchema (no relationshipName) → renderer: ObjectFieldInspector "Relationship name" InspectorTextField`.
  - Not touched here: removing the control and declaring the key in the spec are two different contract answers, and the file surface of this claim is the formula editor.
  - Dedupe words: `relationshipName`, `Relationship name lookup inspector`, `unrecognized_keys relationshipName`, `lookup relationship name 422`.
- **Comment drift, outside this claim's file surface.** The `RETIRED_FIELD_KEYS` note in `previews/object-fields-io.ts` quotes the migration as `patchDef({ expression: …, formula: undefined })`. After this PR the editor writes the next definition without the key, and the rest of that sentence still holds. Suggested words: "the first edit commits the spec key and removes the alias (the editor writes the next definition without `formula`)". Carrier: none.
- The `def.expression ?? def.formula` seed of the editor is the migration objectui#6526 ruled for, and it is unchanged.
